claims.text: A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can be introduced into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix through surface or interface engineering.
The nanohierarchical architecture and composition undulation enhance interfacial bonding.
The nanohierarchical architecture and composition undulation enhance material properties.
Introducing the nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation reduces the coefficient of friction relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
Introducing the nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation reduces the wear rate relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The reductions in coefficient of friction and wear rate persist throughout sliding tests from room temperature to 800 °C.
The exact magnitudes of the friction and wear-rate reductions are uncertain.
A controlled comparison of modified and unmodified CoCrFeNi samples can test the intervention by measuring coefficient of friction and wear rate.
